task: I want to improve the codeeditor - the autocomplete is working, but it still not user friendly enough. For example: when TransformStream is selected from autocomplete, insert a usage template like TransformStream<number, number>({ transform(chunk, controller) { ... } }); similarly ReadableStream<number>({ start(controller) { ... } }). Not necessarily auto-insert — a template-of-usage popover dialog where the user selects among available templates is also acceptable.

analysis.objective: Add a generic, data-driven 'usage template' mechanism to the CodeMirror-based code editor so that accepting a built-in TS completion item that carries usage templates shows a popover picker the user can choose from (or decline to insert just the bare identifier), seeded with a small curated set (TransformStream, ReadableStream, and a few other web platform types).
analysis.successDefinition: 1) Mechanism is generic: a completion item can carry zero-or-more usage templates as data attached to the item, and adding a new type's templates requires a data-only change with no edits to the completion source or editor wiring. 2) On accept of an item that has templates, a popover appears listing them; selecting one inserts the full template text at the cursor indentation-aware, and declining/dismissing inserts only the bare identifier. Nothing auto-inserts. 3) Behavior is byte-identical to today when an item has no templates. 4) Curated data covers at least TransformStream and ReadableStream plus a small set (AbortController and other stream variants). 5) The inserted template is syntactically valid JS/TS and indentation-correct at non-zero indent. 6) New unit tests cover the mechanism (attach, popover trigger, choose, decline) and curated data; build (tsc -b) and lint introduce no new errors; existing editor completion tests stay green.
assumptions: The target editor is CodeMirror 6 (confirmed: editorCompletions.ts composes @codemirror/autocomplete sources); the Monaco dependency in package.json is not the sandbox code editor's completion path.

CodeMirror 6 has no built-in 'popover on accept' primitive, so the template popover must be a hand-built editor overlay (ViewPlugin + DOM positioned from editor viewport coordinates) bridged to a React component; focus/dismiss (Escape, click-outside, blur) must be handled in that overlay.

Usage templates are static text curated by hand (concrete generics exactly as in the examples, e.g. TransformStream<number, number>), not generated or inferred by the LanguageService, and not dependent on the CDN window.ts runtime being available.

On accept, constructor entries already carry apply:'' (the identifier is already typed ahead of the open paren), so 'insert bare identifier' is the current accept behavior; template insertion must compute the correct replacement range including the trailing '(' and whitespace.

The editorCompletions.ts module must stay component-free (react-refresh convention, per the repo's own comments), so the React popover lives in a separate component driven through a non-component bridge (e.g. a command/dispatch), keeping the extension wiring unit-testable without a DOM.
A template referencing an undefined symbol (e.g. the ReadableStream example's 'nums') may surface tsLint errors after insertion; this is tolerated as illustrative and is not a gate.
risks: Post-accept popover placement: CodeMirror 6 provides no popover-after-accept primitive, so the overlay must compute cursor pixel coordinates and manage focus; getting coordinate math or focus/dismiss wrong produces a mispositioned or focus-trapping popover.

Replacement-range correctness: constructor accepts already use apply:'' with the identifier left in the doc; naive template insertion could produce malformed output like 'TransformStream(TransformStream<number...' — the range must cover the identifier plus the trailing '('.
Indentation of multi-line templates at nested cursor positions: inserting a 7-line template at a deep indent without re-indenting its body breaks the relative indentation of the inserted code.

React/CodeMirror bridge: putting the popover inside editorCompletions.ts violates the repo's react-refresh component-free convention and breaks its DOM-free unit tests; the React component must be separated behind a bridge.
Regression on the common path: items without templates (the dominant case) must keep current accept behavior exactly; any change to the accept path risks breaking existing completion tests.

Templates that reference undefined locals (e.g. 'nums') trigger tsLint errors on insertion, which users may read as the feature being broken; must decide whether curated templates are self-contained or documented as illustrative.
outOfScope: Auto-insertion of templates on accept — the user explicitly scoped the UX to a popover picker where the user chooses or declines.
Templates for arbitrary user-defined or future types beyond the curated set — the mechanism is built first; only the first curated set (streams + a few) ships, future types add data.
Full lib.dom.d.ts web-platform type coverage — only 'Streams + a few' types are curated, not all global types.
AI/ML-generated or LanguageService-inferred template suggestions — templates are hand-curated static data only.
User-authored / persisted custom templates (saving user templates to localStorage or disk) — not requested.
Changes to the tsCheck LanguageService entrypoint or signature-help behavior — the existing Phase 0-3 completion/signature pipeline stays as-is.
The 5 sandbox service handles (sandboxServiceCompletions) — they remain owned by the sync source and never receive usage templates.
Template behavior for JS (non-TS) mode — usage templates are TS-mode only, since the built-in-type completion source that would carry them is TS-only.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is about editor machinery — completion item data, a popover picker UI, and template insertion inside a CodeMirror editor — with no business entities, rules, or domain workflows a domain expert would recognize.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: a single suggestion in the editor's autocomplete list
static code snippet attached to a completion item showing how to construct/use the symbol
the in-editor overlay listing available usage templates on accept
the editor action confirming a highlighted completion item
the plain symbol name inserted when the user declines templates
the hand-written first collection of templates (streams + a few)
a CodeMirror autocomplete source that produces completion items

discoveryFindings.finding: src/infrastructure/editorCompletions.ts composes three javascriptLanguage.data.of({ autocomplete }) facet entries: scopeCompletionSource(globalThis), sandboxServiceCompletions, and (TS only) builtInTsCompletion. toCompletion(entry) sets `apply: ''` whenever entry.detail?.startsWith('new '). @codemirror/autocomplete is 6.20.3. Completion.apply type is `string | ((view, completion, from, to) => void)` — the function form is the built-in hook for custom accept behavior; its docs require adding the `pickedCompletion` annotation if dispatching a transaction.
discoveryFindings.implication: Use the function-form `apply` on curated items as the popover trigger. Non-curated items keep the existing apply (string/'' default), so the no-template path stays byte-identical.

discoveryFindings.area: Two distinct accept paths for the same type name
discoveryFindings.finding: A curated type like ReadableStream can be accepted from (a) bare-identifier context via getCompletionsAtPosition with apply defaulting to replacing the typed partial with the label; (b) constructor context `new ReadableStream(` short-circuits to constructorSignatureEntries whose apply is '' and passes from=to=context.pos (empty range).
discoveryFindings.implication: 'Decline -> bare identifier' must reproduce each path's current behavior separately. Template insertion needs a range the source does not provide in the constructor case: the apply function must itself compute the replacement span (walk back over `new Name(`).

discoveryFindings.finding: NO existing ViewPlugin/hoverTooltip/showTooltip/tooltip/popover usage anywhere in src/. @codemirror/view 6.43.8 exports showTooltip, Tooltip, TooltipView, ViewPlugin, repositionTooltips.
discoveryFindings.implication: The popover must be built from scratch on @codemirror/view (showTooltip + custom TooltipView hosting the React root, or a ViewPlugin-managed overlay). Plan must include cursor-coordinate computation, focus management, and Escape/click-outside/blur dismissal.

discoveryFindings.finding: editorCompletions.ts header: wiring is a pure function of the language mode so CodeEditor.tsx stays component-only and the wiring is unit-testable without a DOM. eslint uses reactRefresh.configs.vite (only-export-components rule): .tsx files may only export components, .ts files must not export JSX.
discoveryFindings.implication: The React popover component must live in a separate .tsx file under src/components/, while apply/extension/range logic stays in .ts files under src/infrastructure/. A non-component bridge (pure functions / zustand store / event) must carry popover state from .ts to .tsx.

discoveryFindings.area: Built-in type completion data source & per-item metadata
discoveryFindings.finding: Built-in TS completions are generated by the TypeScript LanguageService (tsCheck.getCompletions -> getCompletionsAtPosition + getCompletionEntryDetails), resolving against lib.es2021 + lib.dom + sandboxAmbient. TsCompletionEntry = { name, kind, kindModifiers, sortText, detail? }. The CodeMirror Completion interface has NO free-form data field and is subject to TS excess-property checking on literals.
discoveryFindings.implication: Attach templates by a curated side-map keyed on entry.name (label), consumed in toCompletion/apply — not by extending the Completion object. Keeps the mechanism generic: adding types is data-only.

discoveryFindings.finding: Vitest ^4.1.10; no test environment configured (Node, no jsdom/happy-dom). Completion tests synthesize the environment (globalThis.window = { ts }, stubbed fetch serving lib.d.ts from node_modules). No e2e/playwright harness.
discoveryFindings.implication: Popover DOM cannot be unit-tested in the current environment. Split the mechanism into pure Node-testable logic plus a thin DOM shell; do not promise DOM-level popover tests without adding jsdom/happy-dom.

discoveryFindings.finding: @codemirror/autocomplete ^6.20.3, view ^6.43.8, state ^6.7.1, language ^6.12.4, lint ^6.9.7, commands ^6.10.4, lang-javascript ^6.2.5. TS devDep ~6.0.2 (installed 6.0.3) but runtime LS compiler is 5.4.5 from CDN. Build = tsc -b && vite build; lint = eslint .; test = vitest run. tsconfig.app.json strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, jsx react-jsx.
discoveryFindings.implication: New code must survive tsc -b strict + eslint react-refresh. Tests must tolerate devDep 6.0.3 vs runtime 5.4.5 drift.

discoveryFindings.finding: No usage-template data exists. Closest patterns: serviceCompletions.ts SERVICE_INTERNAL_METHODS (Record<string, readonly string[]> keyed by handle); sandboxAmbient.ts DOM_AUGMENT_TEXT (hand-curated DOM type patches).
discoveryFindings.implication: Create a data module adjacent to builtInTsCompletion.ts (e.g. src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts) exporting `Record<string, UsageTemplate[]>` keyed by type label, mirroring SERVICE_INTERNAL_METHODS. sandboxAmbient DOM_AUGMENT_TEXT is precedent for authoritative stream shapes.

discoveryFindings.finding: @codemirror/autocomplete exports `snippetCompletion(template, completion)` building an apply with ${}-field navigation (snippetKeymap: Tab/Shift-Tab/Escape). No snippet keymap wired into CodeEditor.tsx (spreads completionKeymap/defaultKeymap/closeBracketsKeymap/historyKeymap only).
discoveryFindings.implication: For static, field-less usage templates the plain function-form apply is the more direct fit than snippetCompletion; snippetCompletion + snippetKeymap is available later if templates gain tab-stop fields.

phases.name: Curated usage-template data module (typeUsageTemplates)
phases.goal: Introduce the data-driven foundation of the usage-template mechanism: a UsageTemplate type and a curated USAGE_TEMPLATES: Record<string, UsageTemplate[]> keyed by completion label, covering TransformStream, ReadableStream, WritableStream, and AbortController, mirroring the existing SERVICE_INTERNAL_METHODS curated-record convention so that adding a future type's templates is a data-only change with zero edits to the completion source or editor wiring.
phases.inputs: serviceCompletions.ts SERVICE_INTERNAL_METHODS curated-record convention; sandboxAmbient.ts DOM_AUGMENT_TEXT as precedent for hand-curated DOM type shapes; user's template examples TransformStream<number, number>({ ... }) and ReadableStream<number>({ ... })
phases.expectedResult: New src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts exporting `UsageTemplate { label: string; text: string }` and a non-empty USAGE_TEMPLATES record for the curated types (TransformStream, ReadableStream, WritableStream, AbortController), plus a Node unit test asserting every entry has a non-empty label, non-empty text, and a non-empty template body.

rubric.label: UsageTemplate type and record structure
rubric.ruleStatement: The module exports a `UsageTemplate` type and a `USAGE_TEMPLATES` record typed `Record<string, UsageTemplate[]>`, mirroring the SERVICE_INTERNAL_METHODS curated-record convention so every future type addition is a data-only edit.
passCriteria: `UsageTemplate` is an exported type with exactly the fields `label: string` and `text: string`.
`USAGE_TEMPLATES` is exported from `src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts` and declared with the type annotation `Record<string, UsageTemplate[]>`.
The record values are arrays of template objects, not a flat `Record<string, string>` of raw snippets.
failureExamples: `UsageTemplate` lacks the `label` field or adds required fields beyond `text`.
`USAGE_TEMPLATES` is typed `Record<string, string>` with snippets as bare strings.
The module is not exported, or lives outside `src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts`.

rubric.label: Curated set complete and keyed by completion label
rubric.ruleStatement: The record contains a non-empty entry for every curated type — TransformStream, ReadableStream, WritableStream, AbortController — keyed exactly by the completion label (the bare symbol name) so the picker can look templates up by the accepted item's label.
passCriteria: Record keys include exactly `TransformStream`, `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, `AbortController`.
Each of those four keys maps to a non-empty array of templates.
The record is non-empty (at least 4 entries).
failureExamples: AbortController is missing (only 3 types covered).
A key is misspelled or lowercased (e.g. `readablestream`), so a label lookup would miss.
A curated key maps to an empty array `[]`.

rubric.label: Template text is a real, non-empty construction snippet
rubric.ruleStatement: Every template `text` is a non-empty, realistic code snippet for constructing/using its symbol (consistent with the user's `TransformStream<number, number>({ ... })` and `ReadableStream<number>({ ... })` examples), carrying a template body beyond the bare identifier.
passCriteria: Every `text` is non-empty after trimming.
No `text` equals just the bare symbol identifier — each contains a body (constructor call, method chain, or block).
Stream templates follow the curated construction style, e.g. `new TransformStream<number, number>({ ... })`.
failureExamples: `text` is the bare identifier `"TransformStream"` with no body.
Whitespace-only or empty text.
A placeholder like `"TODO"` or a stub `"..."`.

rubric.label: Node unit test asserts every-entry invariants
rubric.ruleStatement: A Node unit test iterates every entry of USAGE_TEMPLATES and asserts each has a non-empty label, a non-empty text, and a non-empty template body, and passes deterministically.
passCriteria: The test file exists in the expected Node test location.
The test loops over ALL entries of USAGE_TEMPLATES, not a hardcoded one or two types.
Assertions cover non-empty label, non-empty text, and non-empty template body.
The repo test runner passes on repeated runs.
failureExamples: The test only checks TransformStream, leaving the rest unguarded.
No assertion on the `label` or `text` fields.
The test fails to compile or fails when run.

rubric.label: Data-only footprint — no edits outside the data module and its test
rubric.ruleStatement: This phase adds the curated data module and its test only; it leaves the completion source (`serviceCompletions.ts`) and editor wiring untouched so the change is scope-bounded and trivially revertible (rollback-safe).
passCriteria: `git status`/`git diff` shows only `src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts` and its unit test added or modified.
No edits to `serviceCompletions.ts` or any editor/UI wiring files.
`USAGE_TEMPLATES` is not imported or consumed by the completion source in this phase.
failureExamples: The template popover picker was wired into the editor as part of this phase (out of scope — a later phase).
`serviceCompletions.ts` was modified to read `USAGE_TEMPLATES`.
Unrelated files were changed in the same diff.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is an incomplete curated set or placeholder template text — diff the record keys against the four required types and make each `text` a real constructor-call snippet in the same style as `TransformStream<number, number>({ ... })`, keeping the diff confined to the data module and its test.

phases.name: Pure usage-template lookup, replacement-range, and insert logic
phases.goal: Build the pure, Node-testable core of the mechanism: resolve usage templates for a completion label, compute the exact replacement range for both accept paths (bare-identifier partial-replacement, and constructor `new Name(` walk-back where apply from==to==pos), produce the bare-identifier insert that reproduces each path's current behavior, and re-indent multi-line template bodies to the cursor line's indent so templates are indentation-correct at nested cursor positions.
phases.inputs: typeUsageTemplates.ts data shape (phase usage-template-data); discovery finding on the two accept paths and apply from/to semantics (from==to==pos in the constructor case, so the replacement span must be computed, not trusted from the source)
phases.expectedResult: New src/infrastructure/usageTemplateInsert.ts with zero-DOM pure functions (template lookup by label, decline/bare-insert per accept path, template-insert text + replacement range, template-body re-indent), covered by Node unit tests: constructor `new TransformStream(` walk-back, bare-identifier partial replacement, and multi-line body at a nested indent.

rubric.label: Usage-template lookup by completion label
rubric.ruleStatement: Given a completion label, the module resolves the usage templates attached to that label from the phase's data input, and returns an empty result for labels with none — without throwing and without touching any editor state.
passCriteria: lookup('TransformStream') returns the curated template(s) for that label from the typeUsageTemplates data shape input
a label that exists in data but has no attached templates returns an empty list (never undefined and never throws)
an unknown label (e.g. 'DoesNotExist') returns an empty list and does not throw
repeated lookups of the same label return identical results (deterministic, no state mutation)
failureExamples: throws or returns undefined for an unknown or template-less label
returns a template belonging to a different label
mutates or sorts the caller's template data as a side effect

rubric.label: Bare-identifier insert reproduces both accept paths' current behavior
rubric.ruleStatement: Declining templates produces a bare-identifier insertion whose inserted text and replacement range exactly reproduce the pre-phase behavior on BOTH accept paths (partial-replacement and constructor walk-back), with zero template text leaking in.
passCriteria: on the bare-identifier partial-replacement path, insert text is exactly the symbol name and the replacement range spans only the partial identifier typed so far

on the constructor path, insert text is exactly the symbol name and the replacement range covers only the partially-typed identifier (computed from < to), leaving the `new ` prefix and following context intact
a unit test asserts the resulting document text matches expected behavior (e.g. `new Trans` -> `new TransformStream`) with no stray or duplicated characters
the bare-insert result contains no snippet/template body text
failureExamples: declining a template still inserts `new Name(` or template body text
duplicates the `new ` prefix
produces a replacement range where from > to or from == to
swallows adjacent non-identifier characters in the document

rubric.label: Constructor replacement span is computed, not trusted from the source
rubric.ruleStatement: For the constructor accept path where apply from==to==pos, the replacement span is computed by walking back over the identifier from the cursor, never trusted from the (degenerate) source range.
passCriteria: given source ending in `new Trans` with cursor at end, the computed from-to span covers exactly `Trans`
walk-back stops at the identifier/word boundary and does not swallow the `new ` keyword
the walk-back is a pure function of (source, pos) — no editor or CodeMirror types in its signature
inserting `new TransformStream(` via this span yields exactly one `new ` prefix, no duplication
a Node unit test covers the constructor walk-back scenario and asserts exact expected text
failureExamples: returns from == pos (no walk-back), yielding `new new TransformStream(` on accept
walk-back swallows the `new ` keyword into the span
off-by-one leaves or drops a trailing character of the typed identifier
fails on an uppercase-first identifier or when the identifier is already complete

rubric.label: Multi-line template bodies re-indent to cursor-line indent
rubric.ruleStatement: Multi-line template bodies are re-indented so that every line aligns with the cursor line's indent while preserving each line's original relative indentation, as a pure function of (body, cursorIndent).
passCriteria: inserting a template at a nested cursor (e.g. inside a 4-space-indented block) yields body lines each prefixed with that indent, preserving relative offsets between lines
the first line keeps its content intact; no spurious indentation is added when the cursor indent is 0 (top level)
a Node unit test covers a multi-line body at a nested indent and asserts the exact expected output text
re-indent never mixes tabs and spaces and never introduces trailing whitespace
failureExamples: all lines collapse to the first line's indent, losing the body's relative structure
only the first line is re-indented while continuation lines stay put
a top-level (indent 0) insert gains stray leading whitespace
re-indent depends on editor/DOM state instead of the (body, cursorIndent) inputs

rubric.label: Zero-DOM pure module covered by Node unit tests
rubric.ruleStatement: The module is a zero-DOM, pure-function module that runs under plain Node with no editor host, is repeatable and side-effect-free, and has Node unit tests covering the three named scenarios.
passCriteria: src/infrastructure/usageTemplateInsert.ts imports no CodeMirror/@codemirror/* or DOM (no document/window) symbols

all exported functions take plain data (strings, numbers, plain objects) and are repeatable: calling any function twice with the same input yields identical results with no observable side effects on caller objects or module state
a Node unit test file exists and passes via the standard test runner with no jsdom or mocked DOM
tests cover all three named scenarios: constructor walk-back, bare-identifier partial replacement, and multi-line body at a nested indent
failureExamples: module imports EditorView or references document/window
a function mutates a caller-provided object or caches results across calls in a way that changes output
the test file requires jsdom/a DOM host to run
one of the three named scenarios has no test

phases.healerHint: The constructor accept path is where this phase usually dies — an executor that trusts from==to==pos and skips the walk-back yields `new new TransformStream(` — so make the walk-back its own pure (source, pos) function, assert computed from < pos, and write the `new ` prefix-preservation test first before touching any other path.

phases.name: Popover state bridge between completion logic and React UI
phases.goal: Provide the non-component state carrier that lets the .ts completion apply hook open a template popover and the .tsx React component render/close it, keeping the extension wiring component-free (the repo's react-refresh convention documented in editorCompletions.ts) and Node-unit-testable without a DOM.
phases.boundedContext: popover state bridge (editor completion mechanism <-> editor UI)
phases.inputs: UsageTemplate type from usage-template-data; the only-export-components react-refresh convention enforced by eslint and the component-free wiring pattern in editorCompletions.ts
phases.expectedResult: New src/infrastructure/popoverBridge.ts (plain module/zustand store, no React imports) exposing open/close/update for a template popover carrying the templates list plus an anchor/range captured at accept time, with a subscribe API, plus Node unit tests covering open/close/update/clear lifecycle; eslint react-refresh passes.

rubric.label: Component-free bridge module
rubric.ruleStatement: The bridge must be a plain module (zustand store) with no React imports, no JSX, and no hooks, and it must not break the repo's only-export-components react-refresh convention — eslint react-refresh must pass on it as-is.
passCriteria: src/infrastructure/popoverBridge.ts is a .ts file (not .tsx) with no `import ... from 'react'` and no JSX anywhere in it.
No React hooks (useState/useEffect/useRef/useSyncExternalStore) appear in the file.
Running eslint react-refresh against the file reports zero errors for the module.
A .tsx component can import the store without the only-export-components rule firing.
failureExamples: popoverBridge.ts is a .tsx file or contains `import { useState } from 'react'`.
The bridge is written as a custom hook (e.g., useTemplatePopover) that exports non-component values.
eslint react-refresh fails with 'fast refresh only works when a file only exports components'.

rubric.label: Open/close/update/clear lifecycle
rubric.ruleStatement: The store must expose open, close, update, and clear actions whose transitions are idempotent and repeatable, always terminating in a known pristine state, with Node unit tests covering every transition including double-calls (repeatability and rollback safety).
passCriteria: open(payload) transitions to an open state carrying the payload; calling it twice yields the same state with no error.
close() and clear() both restore the documented default (pristine) state; calling close() twice is safe and does not throw.
update() modifies only the intended field and does not reopen a closed popover.
Unit tests exercise open, close, update, and clear, including repeated open/close cycles that always end pristine with no accumulated anchor/template residue.
failureExamples: close() leaves stale template/anchor data readable afterward.
Double-close or double-open throws or mutates state unexpectedly.
Tests cover only the happy-path open→read and skip close, update, or clear entirely.

rubric.label: Anchor and templates carried at accept time
rubric.ruleStatement: The open action must carry BOTH the curated templates list and the anchor/range captured at accept time as distinct fields, and update() must preserve the anchor until the popover closes, because the .tsx component needs it to position the overlay.
passCriteria: The open action accepts a payload with distinct templates and anchor/range fields.
The store's public state type exposes separate properties for the templates list and the anchor/range.
A unit test asserts the anchor value is unchanged after an update() call.
close/clear wipe the anchor so a later accept starts from a fresh anchor.
failureExamples: Templates and anchor are merged into one field, or the anchor is derived from the templates list.
update() overwrites the anchor with the new templates' position.
open() drops or never stores the anchor, leaving the component unable to position the popover.

rubric.label: Subscribe API for the React component
rubric.ruleStatement: The bridge must expose a subscribe API usable from the .tsx component without importing React, returning an unsubscribe that stops notifications, with all of it verifiable in a Node test with no DOM.
passCriteria: subscribe(cb) returns an unsubscribe function.
A subscriber callback fires on open, update, and close/clear state changes.
After calling the returned unsubscribe, further mutations do not invoke that callback (no listener leak).
The lifecycle tests run in the Node test runner with no window/document usage and pass without jsdom.
failureExamples: subscribe returns void or throws without returning an unsubscribe.
Listeners keep firing after unsubscribe, leaking callbacks.
The implementation reads window/document, so tests require a DOM or jsdom to pass.

rubric.label: Typed against UsageTemplate data
rubric.ruleStatement: The templates carried by the bridge must be typed with the UsageTemplate type imported from usage-template-data — no any/unknown in the payload — so the curated set flows from the data module through the bridge without casts or silent type drift.
passCriteria: popoverBridge.ts imports UsageTemplate from the usage-template-data module's public entry.
The templates field is declared as UsageTemplate[] (or readonly) — not any or unknown.
tsc compiles the module and its tests cleanly.
A unit test constructs a real UsageTemplate value, passes it through open→update, and asserts it is returned unchanged.
failureExamples: Templates typed as `any[]`, `unknown[]`, or a locally duplicated struct instead of the shared UsageTemplate.
The type is imported from a private/deep file whose export is unstable.
Tests cast the payload to silence a type error rather than using a genuine UsageTemplate value.

phases.healerHint: Most likely the bridge gets written as a React hook or imports React/JSX and trips the react-refresh only-export-components rule — fix by stripping all React imports and hooks into a plain store that exports only open/close/update/clear and subscribe, then re-run the eslint react-refresh gate.

phases.name: Wire usage-template accept behavior into builtInTsCompletion
phases.goal: Assign the function-form apply to curated completion items so that accepting a template-bearing item opens the template popover via the bridge without inserting anything, while items with no templates keep today's byte-identical accept behavior (apply:'' for constructor entries, label-replacement for bare identifiers), keeping existing completion tests green.
phases.inputs: usageTemplateInsert lookup/decision functions (phase usage-template-insert-logic); popoverBridge open API (phase usage-template-popover-bridge); current toCompletion/apply semantics and test pins in builtInTsCompletion.ts and builtInTsCompletion.test.ts
phases.expectedResult: builtInTsCompletion.ts modified so curated labels get a function-form apply that resolves templates and calls bridge.open with no doc mutation; extended unit tests prove curated items trigger the bridge and non-curated items (the dominant case) keep current behavior; existing builtInTsCompletion.test.ts stays green.
phases.compensation: Restore the previous toCompletion (non-function apply, '' for constructor entries) in builtInTsCompletion.ts; the curated side-map and bridge go unused and accept behavior reverts to the pre-phase state — existing tests already pin the old apply values, so this is a clean revert.

rubric.label: Curated items switch to function-form apply
rubric.ruleStatement: Every curated completion item must carry a function-form apply that is assigned by resolving the curated label set through the insert-logic — never by hand-wiring per-symbol branches that duplicate the decision.
passCriteria: Curated labels are identified via the usageTemplateInsert lookup (the phase input), not a new hardcoded if/switch on symbol name inside builtInTsCompletion.ts
For each curated label, `apply` is a function (`typeof apply === 'function'`), never a string
The apply function delegates template resolution to the usageTemplateInsert lookup/decision functions; it does not re-implement the decision
failureExamples: apply stays a plain string for curated items, so the popover can never open
apply is a function but gated behind a bespoke per-symbol branch that duplicates the insert-logic decision
A curated item is missing apply entirely, so CodeMirror falls back to plain label insertion

rubric.label: Accepting a curated item inserts nothing
rubric.ruleStatement: Invoking the function-form apply for a curated item must open the popover and return without changing the editor document — no completion string CodeMirror could commit, no deferred insert, and no transaction dispatch.
passCriteria: The apply function returns undefined/null so CodeMirror performs no insertion
Unit test invokes the apply with a fake state and asserts the document and selection are unchanged afterward
Test invokes apply twice and asserts still no doc mutation (repeatability of accept)
failureExamples: apply returns a string, so CodeMirror inserts the identifier before or alongside the popover
apply dispatches a transaction/mutation on the doc before calling bridge.open
Test only asserts bridge.open was called and never asserts doc state, leaving an insert undetected

rubric.label: Popover bridge is opened with the resolved templates
rubric.ruleStatement: On accept of a curated item, popoverBridge.open is called exactly once with the template payload produced by the insert-logic — not with a hardcoded stub, a guessed list, or nothing.
passCriteria: The apply resolves templates via usageTemplateInsert and passes that result (not a literal stub) to bridge.open
Unit test mocks the bridge and asserts open is called with the expected template list/decision payload for a curated symbol
Test asserts open is invoked exactly once per accept
failureExamples: bridge.open is never called, so no popover ever appears
bridge.open is called with a hardcoded dummy array that ignores the insert-logic result
bridge.open is invoked multiple times for a single accept

rubric.label: Non-curated accept behavior is byte-identical to pre-phase
rubric.ruleStatement: Items without curated templates must keep today's accept semantics exactly — apply:'' for constructor entries, label-replacement for bare identifiers — and existing builtInTsCompletion.test.ts pins must remain unmodified and green, so the phase changes nothing for the dominant non-curated case.
passCriteria: Constructor entries still use string apply:''; bare identifiers still insert/replace with their label
No function-form apply is introduced on non-curated paths
The existing builtInTsCompletion.test.ts pins are not modified (diff shows only added tests), and the full suite passes unchanged
failureExamples: Constructor entries accidentally get a function-form apply, changing their accept
Bare-identifier replacement text no longer equals the label
A refactor of toCompletion rewrote the pinned apply strings, forcing edits to existing test expectations

rubric.label: Curated label with no templates degrades to bare identifier
rubric.ruleStatement: When the insert-logic resolves zero templates for a curated label, the apply must insert the bare identifier and must NOT open an empty popover — a dead accept or a blank overlay is a correctness failure.
passCriteria: A curated label whose lookup returns an empty template list is covered by a unit test
That test asserts bridge.open is NOT called and the label is inserted/replaced (or the function-form apply returns the label string)
The fallback path is reachable without throwing
failureExamples: An empty template list still triggers bridge.open with an empty payload, rendering a blank popover
An empty template list makes the apply return undefined, so accepting inserts nothing at all (dead key)
The fallback throws when the lookup returns an empty array

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is the curated apply returning the bare label (or undefined) instead of delegating to bridge.open — fix by having the curated branch resolve templates through usageTemplateInsert, call bridge.open with the result, return no value, and keep every non-curated apply string byte-for-byte so the existing suite stays green.

phases.name: Template popover overlay and React picker in CodeEditor
phases.goal: Render the template popover end-to-end: a CodeMirror overlay positioned from accepted-cursor viewport coordinates hosting a React picker listing the available usage templates, where choosing one inserts the template text via the pure insert logic (dispatching a transaction with the pickedCompletion annotation) and declining or dismissing (Escape/click-outside/blur) inserts only the bare identifier; items without templates never show the popover and nothing auto-inserts.
phases.boundedContext: editor UI integration (CodeMirror overlay + React picker)
phases.inputs: popoverBridge subscription (phase usage-template-popover-bridge); usageTemplateInsert choose/decline functions (phase usage-template-insert-logic); CodeEditor.tsx keymap/mount structure; @codemirror/view 6.43.8 showTooltip/TooltipView/ViewPlugin primitives (no existing tooltip/popover infra in src/, so built from scratch)
phases.expectedResult: Accepting a template-bearing completion shows a positioned popover listing the templates; choose inserts the full template text (indentation-aware) and decline/dismiss inserts the bare identifier; the React picker lives in its own .tsx file under src/components/ (react-refresh compliant), CodeEditor.tsx mounts it and registers the overlay; build (tsc -b) and lint pass.
phases.compensation: Remove the overlay registration and the React picker mount from CodeEditor.tsx; the bridge and pure insert logic remain in src but are unused, and to fully revert also drop the bridge.open call added in usage-template-accept-wiring — the editor then returns to the pre-popover accept behavior.

rubric.label: Popover gated to template-bearing items; nothing auto-inserts
rubric.ruleStatement: The popover only ever appears for a completion item that actually carries usage templates, and accepting an item without templates inserts nothing beyond the standard accept — never template text, never a stray overlay.
passCriteria: Accepting a completion item with zero usage templates does not render the overlay.
Accepting a template-less item inserts no extra text beyond the plain completion accept (no auto-inserted snippet).
Code inspection: the overlay / bridge.open call is guarded by a check that the accepted item's usageTemplates collection is non-empty.
A template-bearing item and a template-less item accepted at the same cursor position behave differently (overlay appears vs. does not appear).
failureExamples: Every accept shows the popover, including completions with no templates.
Accepting a plain identifier unexpectedly auto-inserts template body text.
The bridge.open call fires unconditionally on accept.

rubric.label: Choosing a template inserts the full template text, indentation-aware
rubric.ruleStatement: Picking a template from the picker routes through usageTemplateInsert.choose and inserts the complete template source into the document at the accepted cursor, re-indented to the current line's indentation level, via a transaction carrying the pickedCompletion annotation.
passCriteria: Choosing a template results in the document containing the full template text (every line, exact content), not a truncated or summarized version.
The inserted block is re-indented to match the indentation of the line where the completion was accepted.
Code inspection: the picker's choose handler calls usageTemplateInsert.choose, and the transaction is dispatched with the pickedCompletion annotation.
After the insert, the popover is dismissed and no further accept routing fires.
failureExamples: Only a comment or the first line of the template is inserted.
The inserted text is pasted at column 0 regardless of the current indentation.
The picker bypasses the pure insert logic and hand-builds its own transaction without the pickedCompletion annotation.

rubric.label: Decline and every dismiss path insert only the bare identifier
rubric.ruleStatement: Declining (Escape) and dismissing the popover (click-outside, blur) each route through usageTemplateInsert.decline and leave the document containing exactly the bare identifier — template text must not appear through any dismissal path.
passCriteria: Pressing Escape while the popover is open inserts exactly the bare identifier (the plain symbol name).
Clicking outside the popover inserts exactly the bare identifier.
Blurring the editor/document while the popover is open inserts exactly the bare identifier.
Code inspection: the picker's decline handler and the overlay's dismiss handling both call usageTemplateInsert.decline; no dismissal path triggers choose or auto-inserts template text.
failureExamples: Escape closes the popover but inserts nothing, losing the identifier.
Click-outside inserts the template body instead of the bare identifier.
One dismissal path (e.g., blur) is unwired and leaves the popover stuck or the document empty.

rubric.label: Overlay positioned from accepted-cursor viewport coordinates
rubric.ruleStatement: The CodeMirror overlay is positioned from the accepted cursor's viewport coordinates delivered by the popoverBridge subscription — it anchors to those coordinates rather than to a hardcoded or arbitrary location.
passCriteria: Code inspection: the overlay reads its anchor/position from the coordinates in the popoverBridge subscription payload.
The overlay appears near the accepted completion's location (anchored at/near the cursor) rather than at a fixed screen corner.
Accepting completions at different cursor positions moves the overlay accordingly.
failureExamples: The overlay position is hardcoded (constant x/y) and ignores the bridge-supplied coordinates.
The overlay renders at a fixed screen corner or top-left regardless of the cursor.
The subscription payload coordinates are subscribed to but never read by the overlay.

rubric.label: React picker in its own react-refresh-safe .tsx; mounted by CodeEditor.tsx
rubric.ruleStatement: The picker component lives in its own .tsx file under src/components/, is react-refresh compliant (not merged into CodeEditor.tsx in a way that breaks fast refresh), and CodeEditor.tsx mounts it and registers the overlay with the editor state.
passCriteria: The picker is defined in its own .tsx file under src/components/ rather than inline in CodeEditor.tsx.
The new file's exports are react-refresh compatible (no module-level side effects co-located with the component export that force full reloads).
CodeEditor.tsx imports the picker and mounts it inside the overlay, and registers the overlay extension on the editor.
failureExamples: The picker markup is inlined directly into CodeEditor.tsx.
The new .tsx file mixes a component export with module-level side effects, breaking react-refresh (full reload on every edit).
The overlay is never registered, so no overlay renders despite the picker existing.

rubric.label: Build/lint green; compensation revert restores pre-popover behavior
rubric.ruleStatement: With the phase wired in, tsc -b and lint pass; and the phase's stated compensation (removing the overlay registration and picker mount from CodeEditor.tsx) produces a still-clean build/lint and restores the pre-popover accept behavior — evidence the phase is reversible without leaving dangling references.
passCriteria: tsc -b succeeds with the overlay and picker wired into CodeEditor.tsx.
The repo's lint command passes with no new errors from the new picker file or the CodeEditor.tsx changes.

In a scratch worktree, applying the compensation (removing the overlay registration and the picker mount from CodeEditor.tsx) yields a green build/lint with no dangling imports, and accepting a template-bearing completion inserts the bare identifier directly with no overlay.
failureExamples: tsc -b or lint fails with the phase in place.
Reverting leaves an import of the removed picker or overlay, breaking the build.
After the revert the editor still registers or renders the overlay, so behavior does not return to pre-popover accept.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is the overlay appearing at a hardcoded or zero position, or appearing for every completion, because the viewport anchor coordinates and the non-empty-templates gate are wired by assumption — fastest fix is to add a render-time guard asserting non-empty usageTemplates and finite coordinates, then trace the bridge.open call site so it fires only for template-bearing items.

successCriteria: 1) Mechanism is generic: a completion item can carry zero-or-more usage templates as data attached to the item, and adding a new type's templates requires a data-only change with no edits to the completion source or editor wiring. 2) On accept of an item that has templates, a popover appears listing them; selecting one inserts the full template text at the cursor indentation-aware, and declining/dismissing inserts only the bare identifier. Nothing auto-inserts. 3) Behavior is byte-identical to today when an item has no templates. 4) Curated data covers at least TransformStream and ReadableStream plus a small set (AbortController and other stream variants). 5) The inserted template is syntactically valid JS/TS and indentation-correct at non-zero indent. 6) New unit tests cover the mechanism (attach, popover trigger, choose, decline) and curated data; build (tsc -b) and lint introduce no new errors; existing editor completion tests stay green.

Curated usage-template data module (typeUsageTemplates): New src/infrastructure/typeUsageTemplates.ts exporting `UsageTemplate { label: string; text: string }` and a non-empty USAGE_TEMPLATES record for the curated types (TransformStream, ReadableStream, WritableStream, AbortController), plus a Node unit test asserting every entry has a non-empty label, non-empty text, and a non-empty template body.

Pure usage-template lookup, replacement-range, and insert logic: New src/infrastructure/usageTemplateInsert.ts with zero-DOM pure functions (template lookup by label, decline/bare-insert per accept path, template-insert text + replacement range, template-body re-indent), covered by Node unit tests: constructor `new TransformStream(` walk-back, bare-identifier partial replacement, and multi-line body at a nested indent.

Popover state bridge between completion logic and React UI: New src/infrastructure/popoverBridge.ts (plain module/zustand store, no React imports) exposing open/close/update for a template popover carrying the templates list plus an anchor/range captured at accept time, with a subscribe API, plus Node unit tests covering open/close/update/clear lifecycle; eslint react-refresh passes.

Wire usage-template accept behavior into builtInTsCompletion: builtInTsCompletion.ts modified so curated labels get a function-form apply that resolves templates and calls bridge.open with no doc mutation; extended unit tests prove curated items trigger the bridge and non-curated items (the dominant case) keep current behavior; existing builtInTsCompletion.test.ts stays green.

Template popover overlay and React picker in CodeEditor: Accepting a template-bearing completion shows a positioned popover listing the templates; choose inserts the full template text (indentation-aware) and decline/dismiss inserts the bare identifier; the React picker lives in its own .tsx file under src/components/ (react-refresh compliant), CodeEditor.tsx mounts it and registers the overlay; build (tsc -b) and lint pass.
deferred: Auto-insertion of templates on accept — the user explicitly scoped the UX to a popover picker where the user chooses or declines.
Templates for arbitrary user-defined or future types beyond the curated set — the mechanism is built first; only the first curated set (streams + a few) ships, future types add data.
Full lib.dom.d.ts web-platform type coverage — only 'Streams + a few' types are curated, not all global types.
AI/ML-generated or LanguageService-inferred template suggestions — templates are hand-curated static data only.
User-authored / persisted custom templates (saving user templates to localStorage or disk) — not requested.
Changes to the tsCheck LanguageService entrypoint or signature-help behavior — the existing Phase 0-3 completion/signature pipeline stays as-is.
The 5 sandbox service handles (sandboxServiceCompletions) — they remain owned by the sync source and never receive usage templates.
Template behavior for JS (non-TS) mode — usage templates are TS-mode only, since the built-in-type completion source that would carry them is TS-only.

template-snippet-tabstops — Fails YAGNI gate 2 (needed now): curated templates are static and field-less, so the plain function-form apply already covers them; snippetCompletion's ${}-field navigation would additionally require wiring snippetKeymap into CodeEditor.tsx's keymap list for a feature no phase needs. Revisit only if templates gain tab-stop fields.

dom-popover-e2e-tests — Fails YAGNI gate 2 (needed now): the repo has no jsdom/happy-dom test environment and no playwright harness, and the mechanism is already split so all decision/range/insert logic is Node-testable; adding a DOM test environment is a cross-cutting infra change not required by the objective's success gates. The DOM shell remains code-reviewed instead.

broad-template-curation — Fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for) and gate 2 (needed now): the user scoped curation to the streams-plus-a-few set. The mechanism is data-driven, so templates for arbitrary or future types are a data-only addition later with zero source/wiring changes.
user-persisted-custom-templates — Fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): saving user-authored templates to localStorage or disk was explicitly out of scope in the scoping answers.

auto-insertion-on-accept — Fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): the user explicitly scoped the UX to a popover picker where the user chooses or declines; nothing auto-inserts. Building auto-insert would contradict the scoping answer.

js-mode-templates — Fails YAGNI gate 2 (needed now): usage templates are TS-mode only because the built-in-type completion source that would carry them is TS-only; there is no JS-mode consumer, so deferring blocks nothing.
